intro: Hi again! This lesson builds your first useful word bank: everyday things and people, numbers from 1 to 20, and simple colours and adjectives. Warm-up: name one thing you can see near you right now — in English, if you can!
teachingNotes: Teach words in small groups with an Indonesian gloss.
Numbers 13–19 end in -teen; learners confuse thirteen/thirty, fifteen/fifty — stress -TEEN.
Adjectives come BEFORE nouns in English (a red car = mobil merah); Indonesian puts them after.
Accept British or American spellings (colour/color, grey/gray).

keyPoints.title: Everyday nouns
keyPoints.explanation: People: mother, father, friend, teacher. Places: house, school, office, market. Things: phone, book, table, water.

examples.en: a friend, a teacher, a house
a phone, a book, a table

keyPoints.title: Numbers 1–20
keyPoints.explanation: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, then thirteen to nineteen with -teen, and twenty.

keyPoints.title: Colours and adjectives go before the noun
keyPoints.explanation: Colours: red, blue, green, yellow, black, white. Adjectives: big, small, new, old, hot, cold. Say 'a red car', not 'a car red'.

guidedPractice.hint: The colour comes first in English.

blocks.text: Start with words you use every day: **people**, **places** and **things**. Learn each one with *a* or *an* so you remember how to use it.

id.text: Mulailah dari kata yang kamu pakai setiap hari: **orang**, **tempat** dan **benda**. Pelajari bersama *a* atau *an* supaya ingat cara memakainya.

rows.en: a mother, a father, a friend, a teacher
a house, a school, an office, a market
a phone, a book, a table, a bottle of water

blocks.text: One to twelve have their own names. **Thirteen to nineteen** end in **-teen**. Twenty is **twenty**. Put the stress on *-TEEN* (thir-TEEN) so people don't hear *THIR-ty* (30).

id.text: Satu sampai dua belas punya nama sendiri. **Thirteen sampai nineteen** berakhiran **-teen**. Dua puluh adalah **twenty**. Beri tekanan pada *-TEEN* (thir-TEEN) supaya tidak terdengar *THIR-ty* (30).

rows.id: tiga belas, lima belas, delapan belas

blocks.prompt: How do you write 15 in words?

blocks.text: Indonesian says *mobil merah*; English says **a red car**. Colours (red, blue, green, yellow, black, white) and other adjectives (big, small, new, old, hot, cold) come **before** the noun and never take -s.

id.text: Bahasa Indonesia bilang *mobil merah*; bahasa Inggris bilang **a red car**. Warna (red, blue, green, yellow, black, white) dan kata sifat lain (big, small, new, old, hot, cold) diletakkan **sebelum** kata benda dan tidak pernah ditambah -s.

blocks.explain: Colour first, then the noun: a blue bag.

id.explain: Warna dulu, baru kata benda: a blue bag.

id.title: Warna dan sifat diletakkan di depan

blocks.text: These words appear everywhere: prices in a shop (*twelve dollars*), phone numbers read digit by digit (*oh-eight-one-two…*), and describing what you want (*the black one, the big one*).

id.text: Kata-kata ini muncul di mana-mana: harga di toko (*twelve dollars*), nomor telepon yang dibaca per angka (*oh-eight-one-two…*), dan menjelaskan barang yang kamu mau (*the black one, the big one*).

blocks.text: In phone numbers, English speakers often say 0 as 'oh'.

id.text: Dalam nomor telepon, penutur bahasa Inggris sering menyebut 0 sebagai 'oh'.

id.intro: Hai lagi! Pelajaran ini membangun kosakata pertamamu yang berguna: benda dan orang sehari-hari, angka 1 sampai 20, serta warna dan kata sifat sederhana. Pemanasan: sebutkan satu benda yang bisa kamu lihat di dekatmu sekarang — dalam bahasa Inggris, kalau bisa!
